parsed.name: policy_geopolitics_rearmament_critical_minerals
parsed.strategy: Bet that the fastest-moving policy variables in the Oct 12-Nov 13 window are defence budgets (German +30% YoY, NATO glidepath), nuclear-fuel security (DOE HALEU task order, uranium term pricing), critical-minerals nationalism (Section 232 negotiation, government equity stakes in MP/TMQ/INTC), and the AI power/grid bottleneck that policy is subsidising (transformers, turbines, semicap). Every name has a dated Q3 print or confirmed event inside the window, so relative P&L is driven by real numbers, not theme drift. I would be wrong on a de-escalation headline (Ukraine ceasefire, US-China detente, Kazakh acid resolution) or an adverse ruling on executive equity-taking authority, which hits the policy bucket simultaneously.
parsed.objective: Maximise relative P&L versus the Bloomberg WLS index from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-13 via policy-driven defence, nuclear, critical-minerals and AI-power names with dated in-window catalysts.
